title: Current blocking chains
description: Sessions currently blocked by another session, with wait type and wait time, so the DBA can see who holds whom right now.
sql:
SELECT s.session_id,
       r.blocking_session_id,
       s.login_name,
       r.wait_type,
       r.wait_time,
       r.status,
       r.command
FROM sys.dm_exec_sessions AS s
JOIN sys.dm_exec_requests AS r ON r.session_id = s.session_id
WHERE r.blocking_session_id <> 0
ORDER BY r.wait_time DESC
expected_impact: Minimal; short reads over DMVs only, no locks or waits are introduced.

title: Deadlocks from the system_health ring buffer
description: Recent deadlock graphs retained by the system_health extended-events session, parsed from the ring buffer data as XML.
sql:
SELECT xrb.timestamp AS ring_timestamp,
       CAST(xrb.ring_buffer_data AS xml) AS ring_data
FROM sys.dm_os_ring_buffers AS xrb
WHERE xrb.ring_buffer_type = N'RING_BUFFER_SYSTEM_HEALTH'
ORDER BY xrb.timestamp DESC
expected_impact: Minimal; reads ring buffer data; deadlock graphs may be large.

title: Top resource-consuming queries
description: Completed queries in the lookback window with their cumulative CPU, elapsed, logical-read, and logical-write totals plus the SQL text; the #14 collector ranks the top five per resource category regardless of runtime, so no query is dropped for being fast.
sql:
SELECT qs.total_worker_time,
       qs.total_elapsed_time,
       qs.total_logical_reads,
       qs.total_logical_writes,
       qs.execution_count,
       st.text AS sql_text
FROM sys.dm_exec_query_stats AS qs
CROSS APPLY sys.dm_exec_sql_text(qs.sql_handle) AS st
WHERE qs.last_execution_time >= DATEADD(hour, ?, SYSDATETIME())
expected_impact: Low; aggregated DMV reads plus SQL text handles; filtered to the window.

title: Sessions consuming the most CPU
description: Active sessions ordered by current CPU time, with their running SQL, for spotting high-CPU demand on the instance.
sql:
SELECT TOP (20) s.session_id,
       s.login_name,
       r.cpu_time,
       r.total_elapsed_time,
       st.text AS sql_text
FROM sys.dm_exec_sessions AS s
LEFT JOIN sys.dm_exec_requests AS r ON r.session_id = s.session_id
OUTER APPLY sys.dm_exec_sql_text(r.sql_handle) AS st
WHERE s.session_id > 50
  AND r.cpu_time IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY r.cpu_time DESC
expected_impact: Low; bounded DMV reads and SQL text handles; session CPU signal only.

title: Failed SQL Agent job steps
description: Job steps flagged as failed in the selected window, so the DBA can see repeated or recent job failures at a glance.
sql:
SELECT sj.name AS job_name,
       jh.step_id,
       jh.step_name,
       jh.run_status,
       jh.run_date,
       jh.run_time,
       jh.message
FROM msdb.dbo.sysjobs AS sj
JOIN msdb.dbo.sysjobhistory AS jh ON jh.job_id = sj.job_id
WHERE jh.run_status = 0
  AND jh.run_date >= ?
  AND jh.run_time >= ?
ORDER BY jh.run_date DESC, jh.run_time DESC
expected_impact: Low; reads msdb history tables filtered to the window.

title: SQL Server error log entries
description: Error log lines matching a filter, newest first, so the DBA can flag errors raised in the selected window.
sql:
SELECT xe.log_date,
       xe.process_info,
       xe.text AS error_text
FROM sys.dm_os_error_log AS xe
WHERE xe.text LIKE N'%' + ? + N'%'
ORDER BY xe.log_date DESC
expected_impact: Low; reads the in-memory error log view filtered by text.

title: Databases not ONLINE
description: Databases that are offline, suspect, recovering, or otherwise not available, with their state, so the DBA can flag availability gaps.
sql:
SELECT d.name AS database_name,
       d.state,
       d.state_desc,
       d.user_access_desc,
       d.is_in_standby,
       d.recovery_model_desc
FROM sys.databases AS d
WHERE d.state_desc <> N'ONLINE'
   OR d.is_in_standby = 1
ORDER BY d.name

title: Free space on database file volumes
description: Free space percentage per database file's volume, lowest first, so the DBA can flag storage pressure below 10% free.
sql:
SELECT d.name AS database_name,
       mf.physical_name,
       vs.logical_volume_name,
       vs.total_bytes,
       vs.available_bytes,
       CAST(ROUND(100.0 * vs.available_bytes / vs.total_bytes, 2) AS decimal(8, 2)) AS free_percent
FROM sys.master_files AS mf
JOIN sys.databases AS d ON d.database_id = mf.database_id
CROSS APPLY sys.dm_os_volume_stats(mf.database_id, mf.file_id) AS vs
ORDER BY free_percent ASC
expected_impact: Low; one volume-stat call per database file; no writes.
